stories.title: No oil, no salary: Iraqi state employees are feeling the crunch of the Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Because of the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq cannot export enough oil to fund the country's huge public sector. Protests have already started. Will the Iran war destabilize Iraq again?

stories.title: Cruise ships, quiet towns and an all-day festival: millions flock to eclipse viewing spots across Europe
stories.summary: Beginning in Russia’s remote Arctic north, the eclipse traced an arc over much of western Europe – with the best views in Spain, Iceland and Greenland It was a moment of awe shared by millions across Europe: an eclipse that blocked out the sun, plunging parts of the continent into a daytime darkness in which temperatures dropped and birds suddenly went quiet. Wednesday’s eclipse began in Russia’s remote Arctic north, going on to trace an arc over much of western Europe. From the UK to northern Italy, tens of millions of people turned to the sky as the light of the setting sun was almost completley blocked out. Continue reading...
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Cruise ships, quiet towns and an all-day festival: millions flock to eclipse viewing spots across Europe. Beginning in Russia’s remote Arctic north, the eclipse traced an arc over much of western Europe – with the best views in Spain. Source: The Guardian World.
stories.headline: Cruise ships, quiet towns and an all-day festival: millions flock to eclipse viewing spots across Europe

opening: Beginning in Russia’s remote Arctic north, the eclipse traced an arc over much of western Europe – with the best views in Spain, Iceland and Greenland.

It was a moment of awe shared by millions across Europe: an eclipse that blocked out the sun, plunging parts of the continent into a daytime darkness in which temperatures dropped and birds suddenly went quiet.
body: Wednesday’s eclipse began in Russia’s remote Arctic north, going on to trace an arc over much of western Europe.
From the UK to northern Italy, tens of millions of people turned to the sky as the light of the setting sun was almost completley blocked out.
